## Context / Problem
Code review currently combines workflow-authored built-in criteria with an unconditional project Round-A fan-in and packaged-only overlay/detector selection. This ignores effective disables/retunes, omits activated project DET criteria, ignores project file applicability and explicit dollar budgets, and aborts without partial results when one criterion fails. The approved RP-06 policy corrects these behaviors while preserving hard-won code-review topology and output contracts.

## Approach
Add a code-review strategy adapter that compiles `DiscoveryStagePlan` units from the immutable `CriteriaSnapshot` delivered by S1 and executes them through the shared kernel delivered by S2. Round A keeps the base reviewer and each selected built-in/project criterion exactly once. Project LLM criteria select by effective globs; effective disabled or non-applicable criteria execute zero times with stored reason provenance. Project DET criteria remain outside the LLM fan-in and execute through the detector selector from the same snapshot. Round B remains the existing one-hop, capped base-reviewer recommendation path.

Preserve the authored `code-review.yaml` topology, base-reviewer summary/recommendations payload, per-overlay context overrides, prompt contracts, model-ladder resolution, sequential scheduling, and absence of code-review checkpoints. Code review retains no implicit dollar cap; every positive authored `usd_budget` is enforced and shed units are recorded. Zero remains schema-invalid.

After RP-01 exhausts one local criterion call, retain successes and continue independent criteria. A real blocking finding wins `BLOCK`; otherwise missing blocking-capable coverage returns unsigned `INDETERMINATE`; advisory-only missing coverage may still `PASS`. Systemic configuration/provider setup and cancellation behavior remains fail-safe. Persist the versioned safe discovery trace in the internal code-review journal/sidecar, never in the normal review response or status projection.

During expand-contract, compute the legacy and new deterministic projections from the same calls and record comparison mismatches without issuing duplicate model calls. Approved differences are limited to effective disable/retune, project DET inclusion, project applicability, explicit budget enforcement, and the approved partial-failure verdict policy.

## Testing
Use real workflow producer-to-consumer tests with a stateful fake only at the external model boundary. The oracle is the final typed verdict, exact selected call ids/order, internal trace, and unchanged public response shape. Negative controls pin the base reviewer, one-hop Round B, sequential execution, no checkpoint writes, and no-project-overlay behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] A docs-only diff skips a project criterion scoped to `src/**`, while a matching diff runs it exactly once in Round A; both outcomes are recorded internally without adding trace fields to the review response.
- [x] Effective built-in disable/retune and activated project DET fixtures drive actual code-review selection from one snapshot rather than packaged routing.
- [x] Base-reviewer summary/recommendations, one-hop capped Round B, per-overlay context, model/mode, sequential order, authored YAML topology, and no-checkpoint behavior match the pre-cutover contract when no approved delta applies.
- [x] A positive authored `usd_budget` sheds over-budget units before calls, omission stays uncapped, and zero is rejected by workflow validation.
- [x] With one exhausted local failure, later independent criteria execute and earlier successes survive; dependency-blocked units skip, blocking-capable missing coverage yields `INDETERMINATE` unless a real block exists, and advisory-only missing coverage may pass.
- [x] Systemic setup/configuration failure and cancellation stop remaining work with exact usage accounting and no signed or hollow pass.
- [x] Shadow contract tests use one observed call set and report no differences outside the approved delta allowlist; code-review response and status schemas remain narrow and backward-compatible.
